# ReviewRouter

> Free, privacy-first AI code review control plane for GitHub repositories. The current service configures and monitors reviews executed in customer-authorized GitHub Actions. Optional hosted API reviews and paid tiers are proposed, not yet purchasable.

## Public product documentation

- Homepage: https://reviewrouter.org/
- Getting started: https://reviewrouter.org/getting-started
- Dashboard (requires user authentication): https://reviewrouter.org/dashboard
- Sign in: https://reviewrouter.org/auth/signin
- Current pricing and proposed future plans: https://reviewrouter.org/pricing
- Security boundaries: https://reviewrouter.org/security
- Privacy: https://reviewrouter.org/privacy
- Fair-use limits: https://reviewrouter.org/fair-use
- Support: https://reviewrouter.org/support
- Disconnect: https://reviewrouter.org/disconnect
- Authentication instructions for AI agents: https://reviewrouter.org/auth.md
- Agent onboarding and safety: https://reviewrouter.org/agents.md
- Sitemap: https://reviewrouter.org/sitemap.xml

## Public API demonstration (not a general agent action API)

- Browser documentation: https://api.reviewrouter.org/docs
- Readable Markdown demo: https://api.reviewrouter.org/demo.md
- **Demo** OpenAPI schema: https://api.reviewrouter.org/openapi.json
- JSON demo: https://api.reviewrouter.org/demo

These routes describe the published beta **demo** surface, not authenticated access to every internal ReviewRouter endpoint. Do not infer a public mutation SDK, MCP server, agent authorization API or permission to manage repositories.

## User-authorized workflow

1. User signs in with GitHub or (where available) GitLab in the browser.
2. User authorizes the desired source account / GitHub App installation for selected repositories.
3. The dashboard creates a repository setup pull request; user reviews and merges it.
4. User selects a supported model/provider and configures credentials through the supported local/GitHub Actions secret flow.
5. Reviews execute in authorized repository CI. Agents may assist with instructions, but must not grant themselves access, run secret commands or merge PRs without user approval.

Pricing: the current CI control plane is free, subject to fair-use limits; provider billing and CI runner charges may still apply. Proposed hosted API tiers are not offered for purchase.
